messages:
Lina: FYI customer reported their monthly credits went to 0 right at the reset window, but they swear they had credits remaining. pasted their snippet below.

Lina: Customer pasted: 'We were at ~15% of our monthly credits at 23:50 PST, then at 00:01 PST quota = 0, retrying returns 429 with reason "quota_exhausted". We didn't have any big spike.'

Jonah: pinging billing + infra — looks like a potential timezone/reset edge-case. org id 98765 (no PII).

Carlos: On it. Quick note: our monthly refill job runs at 00:00 UTC (cron), not customer local tz. customers in US/PST see it happen at 16:00 PST on some days depending on DST. That can look like 'disappeared' if their UI expects local day boundary.

Mei: Also check the quota cache TTL and the burst window logic. We have a short window where the quota controller reconciles committed usage + in-flight bursts; if a tenant used burst capacity close to reset time, the reconciliation can yield 0 until the refill job finalizes.

Lina: Customer claims they used no big burst. they provided a single request id: r_93b2f. they included the response headers: "x-rate-limit-remaining: 0" and "x-quota-window-start: 1700000000" (sample).

Carlos: Can you ask them to paste the raw header set? The important fields: x-quota-window-start, x-quota-window-end, x-quota-remaining, x-burst-credits. If the UI only shows a cached remaining value but the backend replaced the window, that mismatch looks like a disappearance.

Lina: Asked customer for headers and last 10 requests. also asked for timezone of org billing setting.

artemis-bot: [automated] billing refill job started: run_id=run-2026-xx-xx-00:00UTC

Mei: To reproduce quickly from our side: query the usage store for the org and the minute buckets around reset. Example SQL we use in support playbook:

```
SELECT bucket_ts, tokens_used, burst_used
FROM org_usage_minutes
WHERE org_id = 98765
AND bucket_ts BETWEEN to_timestamp(1700000000) - interval '10 minutes' AND to_timestamp(1700000000) + interval '10 minutes'
ORDER BY bucket_ts;
```

Mei: Also check the quota-cache table for last_seen, e.g.:

```
SELECT last_seen, cached_remaining, window_start
FROM quota_cache
WHERE org_id = 98765;
```

Carlos: If the cache showed old window_start then a refill could have reset counters before cache invalidation. We surfaced a bug Q-4721 where cache invalidation for monthly refills could be delayed up to 3 minutes under heavy load. That can cause momentary 0 visible to the customer.

Lina: Customer sent the headers. They show: x-quota-window-start: 1700000000, x-quota-window-end: 1702592000, x-quota-remaining: 0, x-burst-credits: 0. They also sent UI screenshot showing '0 credits' at 00:01 local time.

Jonah: Can we check the refill job logs for this run id and the org-specific events?

billing-bot: [automated] refill-run run-2026-xx-xx-00:00UTC completed (duration 38s) — 98765: credits_added=100000, errors=0

Carlos: refill-run claims credits_added succeeded. That suggests customer saw 0 due to a front-end or cache stale read immediately after refill before cache invalidation propagated. We need to confirm timing between refill completion and the customer's first post-reset request (r_93b2f).

Mei: Pulling request logs now. If request r_93b2f hit an edge server that still had old window metadata, the API would return quota_exhausted. We should correlate the request timestamp with the edge node's cache state.

Mei: Found request r_93b2f at 1700000065 (65s after window start). It hit edge e-12. Edge e-12's quota-cache last invalidation timestamp was 1700000020, but the new window_start applied at 1700000000 and the cache still held pre-refill values until 1700000075 on that node. So the edge returned stale 0.

Mei: tl;dr — race between refill job + cache invalidation. edge e-12 served a stale cache for ~75s after refill under rare timing.

Lina: OK — customer-facing explanation: their refill succeeded but a small subset of our edges had stale cache for ~1m, which could show 0 for a request in that window. Apology + fix plan.

Carlos: Immediate mitigation: manual invalidate cache for org 98765 on edge e-12 and e-13, and offer to re-run their failed requests (we can credit back failed tokens). Longer-term: Q-4721 patch to reduce invalidation lag is prioritized for next hotfix. I've created the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/Q-4721 and assigned to eng-sre.

Lina: I posted explanation to the customer, offered to top-up temporary credits while we patch (they accepted), and scheduled a follow-up tomorrow.

Jonah: Customer happy with explanation + proactive top-up. Please add blameless postmortem notes to the internal incident tracker so we can monitor recurrence.

Mei: Added note to infra runbook and created a small monitoring alert: detects when refill-run completes but some edges report pre-refill window_start for >30s.

Carlos: one more thought — we should add a UX hint in the console: "credits are refilled at 00:00 UTC — accounts in other timezones may see the change at local offsets." small doc change.

Lina: Thanks team. closing after follow-up. :white_check_mark:
